trickyParts: A forward merge keeps both sides by design, so a deletion is undone with no conflict for anyone to read. Nothing in this branch's own sweeps would have caught it: `prompts_test.go`'s retired-phrase test scans the composed prompts only, and the skills guard had no CI-line rule. The sweep that proved the deletion in rounds one and three was run before the merge and not again after it.

The guard's condition was the mention direction, not the instruction direction. A rule that fires on any appearance of the words would fail on this pull request's own changelog sentence and on eleven `docs/solutions` supersede notes, each of which names the line precisely in order to say it is gone, and the next author would have to weaken it. The separation that works is grammatical: an instruction puts the line in a subject or object slot a negated mention cannot fill.

The guard's blind spot is anaphora and is documented in its comment: a sentence saying only "the implementer writes it" is not caught. The anchor is the defining sentence such a paragraph opens with, which is what the re-introduced paragraph had and what the control proves it fires on.
deviations: The guard lives in `packages/pi-legion/src/skills-guard.test.ts` rather than beside `oversizedFiles` and `longSkillBodies` in `packages/pi-shared/test/skills-guard.ts`: the rule is about Legion's own pull request body, so it is self-contained in the Legion test as the neighbouring `skip-checks` recipe test is.
